name: Agent Memory and Planning
blurb: How agents remember, plan, and recover.

repos.name: mem0
repos.description: Universal memory layer for AI Agents

repos.name: letta
repos.description: Platform for stateful agents: AI with advanced memory that can learn and self-improve over time.

reading.body:
mem0 holds more than two-thirds of the combined 93,761 stars across these three repositories, making it the dominant open-source choice for giving AI agents persistent memory.

All three projects are active, all carry the Apache-2.0 licence, and all were pushed within the same week ending 2026-08-31. That clustering of recent activity suggests the problem of agent memory is being worked on urgently and in parallel, not handed off to a single winner. The gap in star count between mem0 at 64,384 and letta at 24,498 is large, but letta's focus on stateful, self-improving agents is distinct enough that the two are not straightforward substitutes.

For AI infrastructure, the relevance is indirect but real. Stateful agents that retain memory across sessions make longer and more complex requests to the models they call, which increases per-session compute load compared with memoryless, single-turn interactions. More compute per session means more demand on the hardware and power capacity that sits behind those models. The data does not cover inference costs, energy draw, or deployment scale, so that connection remains qualitative. What the data does confirm is that this is a small field by repository count, openly licensed, and still consolidating.
